newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian financier sees stock market rallying.
newsitem.headline: Indian financier sees stock market rallying.

text.p: Indian financier Uday Kotak, recently named by Euromoney magazine as one of Asia's financial leaders for the 21st Century, said on Wednesday he saw falling real interest rates driving Indian stock markets higher.
"The way people will look at equities and real estate will change," Kotak, vice chairman of Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd, said in an interview.

"Real interest rates are collapsing," he said. "This is an extremely bullish factor for both these markets." He said real interest rates, adjusted for inflation, had halved to eight percent in the past six months -- and would shrink to 4-5 percent in the near term because of declining nominal interest rates and rising inflation.
People who put money into 14 percent term deposits would be left with a negative return of 1.6 percent after inflation ate up 10 percent and taxes took away 5.6 percent, he said.

Kotak Securities Ltd, a group brokerage firm in which investment firm Goldman Sachs holds 28 percent equity, has forecast the benchmark 30-stock Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index to reach 3,800-4,000 by December 1997.
On Wednesday afternoon, the BSE index was trading at 3,459.37, up 76.63 points, or 2.27 percent -- and sharply higher than the three-year low of 2,712.13 on December 4, 1996.

"I'm cautiously optimistic because there are issues like...how the political drama unfolds," Kotak said, adding that with agricultural growth leading the way a clearer picture would depend on bountiful monsoon rains.

The soft-spoken, 37-year-old Kotak is one of India's rising financial stars. He heads a financial services empire with combined turnover of about four billion rupees. The group has tie-ups with Ford Credit International, a subsidiary of Ford Motor Credit Company.

The U.S. firm holds 55 percent in Ford Credit Kotak Mahindra Ltd, in which Indian utility vehicles maker Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) owns 10 percent and the balance 35 percent is held by Kotak Mahindra Finance.
Ford Credit also owns 40 percent equity in Kotak Mahindra Primus, which will finance non-Ford cars in India.
Goldman Sachs holds 28 percent in Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Ltd, another group firm engaged in investment banking.
The group also has a formal agreement with U.S. firm Chubb Corp to set up an insurance firm when the Indian government opens up the state-controlled insurance sector.

Big business breakthroughs come to Kotak at wedding receptions. "Today, we're the largest retail distributor of securities in India," he said, thanks to a 1991 deal he struck after hearing at a wedding party that a diversified firm was selling off its financial services division.

It was also at Kotak's wedding reception in 1985 when Anand Mahindra, now deputy managing director of M&M, became interested in the fledgling financial venture and agreed to put up money and affix their name, a business associate said.
The Mahindras own about 10 percent of the equity in Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd. Harish Mahindra, the father of Anand, is the chairman of Kotak Mahindra but he does not wield any executive powers.
